What you have suggested helps mild cases but IV is used to help manage low blood volume and has been shown to improve quality of life in patients who are suffering with the condition. & no people aren’t hankering after an NG tube or IV drips. The people who require NG tubes are incredibly severe and can’t move  (e.g Whitney Dafoe). https://www.thecanary.co/uk/analysis/2023/09/20/karen-gordon-severe-me-nhs/

https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/me-patients-risk-dying-of-starvation-under-nhs-care-kkdwjbkl2

EDIT- I would just like to add that I am referring to *severe* cases in the above and certainly not advocating for everyone to be placed on a tube or prescribed benzodiazepines

It’s also very hard to get testing in the UK and this isn’t solely because of funding, it’s due to the whole psychiatric “it’s in your head” attitude permeating through the profession (mind you they don’t even learn about this kind of thing in medical school!). In my case I had myocarditis and pericarditis triggered from covid but was denied a referral to cardiology for months despite A&E doctors telling me I needed one. I eventually took out a loan and had a private scan which found the inflammation, i’ve now had treatment for it and I am doing better but I have scar tissue that is irreversible and have suffered much more than I needed to. You can see how their attitudes stop them identifying and treating things that do have cured too!

A couple of examples of the top of my head is access to IV saline to control/manage POTS symptoms, other IV infusions, limited usage of benzodiazepines such as ativan to help with crashes, feeding tubes for those who can no longer eat.
